# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway shows that opened in 2020—a year dramatically cut short by the pandemic—we're reminded of a season that began with artistic ambition before being abruptly halted. The productions that managed to open before Broadway's closure offer a fascinating snapshot of the industry's creative direction just before everything changed.

Leading our rankings is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 82/100 from critics who largely embrace its grittier approach to the beloved musical, though the production hasn't won over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands out with a 78/100 score across 29 reviews, bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama to Broadway for the first time in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race and power remains urgently relevant.

The season's other notable entries reflect Broadway's range: Laura Linney commands the stage in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, a solo adaptation that divides critics even as they universally praise her performance. **Grand Horizons** offers boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, while Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves characteristically polarizing.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the shows from early 2020 represent a strong, if abbreviated, season that showcased both reverent revivals and bold reinterpretations. Whether you're drawn to classical reimaginings, important American dramas, or experimental takes on beloved musicals, these productions offer insight into Broadway's evolving artistic landscape at a pivotal moment in theater history.

# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theatrical ambition cut short by unprecedented circumstances. These five productions—those that managed to open before the industry's historic shutdown—showcase a season defined by bold reinventions of classics and powerful examinations of American identity.

Leading our rankings is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 82/100 from critics who largely embrace its grittier approach to the beloved musical, though the production remains divisive among purists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** scores 78/100 for its long-overdue Broadway debut—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama arrives in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race, power, and military justice remains urgently relevant decades after its creation.

The season's other notable entries include Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), which divides critics despite universal praise for its star, and Bess Wohl's **Grand Horizons** (71/100), a boulevard comedy elevated by Jane Alexander and James Cromwell's performances. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining (68/100) proves the most polarizing entry, with critics split between those celebrating its visceral innovation and those mourning the loss of Jerome Robbins' original choreography.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the abbreviated 2020 season demonstrates Broadway's ongoing tension between preservation and reinvention. Explore our detailed reviews to discover which of these productions best aligns with your theatrical preferences.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a remarkable moment of theatrical renewal and artistic ambition. Following an unprecedented shutdown, the season marked both Broadway's reopening and a creative renaissance, with productions ranging from intimate solo performances to spectacular revivals earning an impressive average critic score of 81/100.

Leading this exceptional class is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance—a technically daring approach that critics hail as unforgettable. Rebecca Frecknall's immersive **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** follows closely, transforming the August Wilson Theatre (formerly Playhouse Theatre) into a fully realized nightclub environment that redefines what Broadway revival can achieve.

The season demonstrates remarkable range: **The Lehman Trilogy** offers epic historical drama spanning 164 years, while intimate works like **Lackawanna Blues** and **Is This a Room** prove that solo performances and verbatim transcripts can be just as theatrically powerful as large-scale productions. Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** and the exuberant pop musical **SIX** show how contemporary reinterpretations can breathe new life into familiar material, while original works like **Pass Over** and **Clyde's** tackle urgent social themes with both gravity and warmth.

Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, immersive spectacle, or intimate character studies, these ten productions showcase the artistic vitality that defined Broadway's return and continue to set the standard for theatrical excellence.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both innovative new voices and essential revivals to the stage. Four years later, many of these productions continue to resonate with audiences and influence contemporary theater.

The season proved particularly strong for musicals with heart. **Kimberly Akimbo** leads our rankings with an impressive 88/100 score, with critics consistently praising its rare ability to balance quirky humor with genuine emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** (86/100) offered audiences a stripped-down Sondheim revival that served as both a fitting tribute to the late composer and a vital reimagining of his work. **A Strange Loop** (86/100), Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, matched that score with its brazenly original exploration of Black queer identity.

The year also marked a significant moment for Pulitzer Prize-winning works on Broadway. Beyond *A Strange Loop*, the season featured revivals of **Topdog/Underdog** and **Between Riverside and Crazy**, alongside new productions of **How I Learned to Drive** and **Cost of Living**—demonstrating Broadway's commitment to bringing celebrated dramatic literature to wider audiences.

With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season delivered consistently high-quality work spanning musicals, straight plays, solo performances, and bold experimental theater. The range encompasses everything from Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt** to Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'**.

Whether you're exploring these shows through cast recordings, published scripts, or hoping to catch any still-running productions or tours, this collection represents some of the strongest theatrical work of the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that premiered in 2023 continue to demonstrate the remarkable artistic vitality of that season, with several productions maintaining their critical acclaim and audience appeal nearly three years later.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's revelatory revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has triumphantly rehabilitated Stephen Sondheim's infamous 1981 flop through emotionally resonant performances and thoughtful staging. The production stands alongside **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, a West End transfer that defies expectations by transcending its source material with technically stunning theatrical craft that appeals far beyond the Netflix series' fanbase.

The 2023 season proves particularly noteworthy for its engagement with American social themes. **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama led by Sarah Paulson, examines inherited racism and family dysfunction with unflinching honesty. **Purlie Victorious: A Non-Confederate Romp Through the Cotton Patch** brings Ossie Davis's 1961 satire back to Broadway with bracing contemporary relevance, while the revival of **Parade** resonates with urgent timeliness in its examination of antisemitism and mob justice.

The season's diversity extends across genres and formats, from Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us**—which brilliantly recounts infiltrating a white nationalist meeting—to the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham**, James Ijames's inventive Hamlet adaptation set at a Black family barbecue. Meanwhile, **Stereophonic**, an immersive three-hour drama set in a 1970s recording studio, continues to earn praise for its masterful theatrical craft.

With an average critical score of 82/100 across these ten productions, the 2023 Broadway season remains a benchmark for artistic excellence and cultural relevance—offering theatergoers compelling reasons to experience these productions while they remain available.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate the remarkable range and vitality of American theater. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 86/100 critical score—showcases everything from intimate character studies to sweeping historical epics, with several shows maintaining their relevance well over a year after opening.

The standout among these productions is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. With 22 reviews and an 89/100 score, critics consistently praise its authentic depiction of the creative process and its status as a theatrical marvel. The play's technical achievements and ensemble performances have set a new benchmark for music-centered drama on Broadway.

Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!** represents another triumph from this class, appearing twice in our rankings with scores of 85/100 and 84/100 across different review collections. This absurdist farce reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist, earning near-universal acclaim for its riotous humor and Escola's fearless comedic vision.

**Operation Mincemeat**, the grassroots sensation that transferred from the West End, proves that inventive storytelling and energetic ensemble work can captivate both critics and audiences, while Amy Herzog's **Mary Jane** offers a quieter but equally powerful counterpoint—an understated examination of maternal devotion in the face of unimaginable challenges.

Whether you're drawn to bold comedic experiments, historically-grounded dramas, or intimate character studies, these 2024 productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As March 2026 arrives, Broadway's 2025 play season continues to resonate with audiences, offering a remarkable blend of bold new voices and reimagined classics. The ten productions featured here represent the strongest critical performers from last year, averaging an impressive 85/100 across reviews.

Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons** leads the pack, earning widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. Arthur Miller's family drama proves as potent as ever in van Hove's stripped-down vision, which critics praise for bringing fresh urgency to the classic text. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** reminds audiences why this quirky musical became a beloved fixture, with critics hailing its joyous spirit and airtight writing as perfectly timed for today's theatrical landscape.

The season's diversity is striking: Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** explores language and identity with sensitivity and intelligence, while **Paddington The Musical** enchants with its remarkably lifelike bear puppet—a genuine theatrical marvel. **Ragtime** returns with renewed timeliness, powered by Joshua Henry's commanding performance, and **The Producers** delivers the belly laughs its reputation promises. Meanwhile, ambitious new works like **Liberation** and the darkly comic **Dead Outlaw** demonstrate Broadway's continued appetite for original storytelling.

Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies, large-scale revivals, or innovative new works, this collection represents the breadth and quality that defined Broadway's 2025 play season. Explore the full list to find your next theatrical experience.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the year's new play offerings remain relatively modest in number, though not without intrigue for theatergoers seeking dramatic fare.

The standout arrival is **Bug**, Tracy Letts' psychological thriller making its long-awaited Broadway debut three decades after its 1996 premiere. The production earns mostly positive reviews from critics, who particularly praise the show's intense performances and claustrophobic tension. With a solid 74/100 average score across 35 reviews, the play demonstrates that Letts' paranoid two-hander about conspiracy theories and deteriorating mental states remains disturbingly relevant for contemporary audiences. The Broadway mounting finally brings this cult favorite to the Great White Way's main stages, where its intimate horror can reach wider audiences.

With only one new play opening so far this year, the 2026 Broadway season presents a notably quiet landscape for dramatic works compared to recent years. This scarcity makes Bug's arrival all the more significant for theater enthusiasts craving non-musical productions. The limited slate reflects broader industry trends, as Broadway continues balancing commercial viability with artistic ambition in an evolving theatrical marketplace.

As spring approaches, theatergoers interested in serious drama will find Bug offering the kind of provocative, performance-driven experience that reminds audiences why intimate plays remain essential to Broadway's ecosystem, even when musicals dominate the marquees. Check individual show pages for detailed reviews, ticket information, and performance schedules as the season progresses.
